concept: A flat-cosmos night world with four held stations, each changing state on the spoken word instead of being redrawn. The orbit picture (Earth, tilted rings, satellites broadcasting) says what is overhead. The sky diagram (a cross-section: Earth's curved surface along the bottom, the phone as a glowing point on it, satellites above) is the lesson's working machine: a stamped pulse travels down, a range line becomes a circle, circles meet, swell together when the phone's clock is off, and snap back to one point when a fourth satellite fixes the clock; it returns for the recap. The two-clocks pair (a clock in orbit above, a clock on the ground below, Earth between) shows quartz against atomic, then speed and gravity pulling the orbit clock's rate, then the clock set slow before launch. The night city with the blue dot opens and closes the film, carries the 300 metre ruler, drifts 10 km in a day and comes home.

stations.note: Earth disc centred about (960, 540), radius about 220, crescent-shaded, night side with a few city lights and one teal point for the phone. Orbit rings around it up to about 1500 wide, tilted, front halves over Earth and back halves behind it. Tags sit on objects (a radius line, an orbit arc, a satellite) at label size 26 to 30. Nothing readable below y 930 (captions).

Plan form (b01, b20, b29): the night city seen from above filling the frame, street grid, blocks with lit windows, a river; the phone in b01 at centre right (about x 1180 to 1560, y 110 to 880). Skyline form (b33, b34): the night skyline along the lower half (towers up to about y 470, ground about y 900), a faint air band across the upper third, the phone at right (about x 1380 to 1720, y 140 to 820). Nothing readable below y 930.

Earth's curved surface across the bottom (crest about y 820 at x 960, falling away to both sides); the phone point at (960, 812). Satellites: A about (430, 230), B about (1490, 200), C about (980, 110); D rises from the right horizon to about (1720, 430) in b23. Range circles centred on the satellites pass through the phone point, large and partly off frame. The phone readout panel (timer, sums, unknown tags) at right about x 1300 to 1800, y 520 to 780; the question at upper left about x 120 to 700, y 380 to 520. Nothing readable below y 930.

Earth disc bottom-left, centre about (420, 1000), radius about 400 (its top near y 600). A satellite on an orbit arc top-left about (560, 230). The orbit clock top-right, centre about (1340, 260), radius about 140, joined by a thin line to the satellite; the ground clock bottom-right, centre about (1340, 700), radius about 140, joined to Earth's surface. Chips beside each clock at about x 1510 to 1880. Gravity well (b27) on the left half under Earth. Phone inset (b30) about x 760 to 1040, y 380 to 860. Nothing readable below y 930.

story.metaphor: None: the literal system, drawn flat. Earth, satellites, a signal, circles, clocks, a phone and its blue dot.
story.setting: One night field: the city below, Earth and its satellites above, a cross-section diagram, and two clocks.
story.arc: A blue dot appears on a night map; the answer is overhead: satellites with atomic clocks broadcasting where and when; travel time gives a distance, a distance gives a sphere, spheres meet at you; the phone's cheap clock breaks it and a fourth satellite fixes it; the satellites' own clocks run fast in orbit and are set slow before launch; the chain replays and the dot lands.

devices.what: The ranging cross-section held from b08 to b24 and replayed in b31 and b32: Earth's curved surface across the bottom with the phone as a glowing teal point, satellites above, a stamped pulse, range lines that sweep into circles (spheres drawn as circles), the overlap ring, two candidate points, all circles swelling together and snapping back to one point.

Two clock faces on one vertical line: the orbit clock on a satellite at the top, the ground clock (the phone's in b19) at the bottom by Earth. Their hands and a small microsecond chip show steady against off, behind, ahead, then in step.

The night city from above with the phone and its blue dot: the dot pulses in, a 300 metre ruler unrolls across the streets, the dot drifts away under a day dial and comes home, wears a soft halo, then lands for good.
Earth in the night field with tilted orbit rings and satellites travelling them; altitude and period as tags on a radius line and an orbit arc, never cards; each satellite pulses as it broadcasts.

The one join material: camera moves between the four stations of the one night world (up from the city to orbit, across to the diagram, on to the clocks), continue joins inside a station, hard cuts only at the open and into the recap.

parts.what: The night city in two forms. Plan: seen from straight above, filling 1920 x 1080: a street grid in line and surface2, blocks in surface with small warm lit windows (accent2 at low opacity), a river in field2 crossing diagonally, a park; it reads as a map. Exposes a position anchor (home) near the centre, a metre scale (pixels per 300 m for the ruler, about 360 px) and a far-edge anchor for the drift. Skyline: a side elevation of the same city along the lower half, towers in surface and surface2 with crescent shading and lit windows, one tall tower at about x 820 whose face can catch a signal (a bounce point anchor), and an air band (a faint muted gradient band in the upper third) that a signal crosses. States: lights_low, lights_up (the close).

The viewer's phone, flat: rounded body in shadow with a surface bezel, crescent shading, offset shadow. Screen states: dark, map (a simplified night map like the city plan), dot (the blue dot in accent4 with a soft pulse ring, offset parameter so it can drift and come home), halo (a soft accent4 uncertainty disc round the dot, size parameter). A readout form for the diagram: a rounded panel (about 500 x 260) that shows a running timer (counts to a given value and stops), and up to four short label rows that light in turn. A quartz clock form: a small cheap clock face that sits on the phone. A mini form (about 280 x 480) for insets. Never a hand or a person.

Earth, flat-cosmos: a crescent-shaded disc (oceans in surface, land in accent4 at low saturation, the night side in shadow with a few warm city lights) with an optional glowing accent4 point for the phone's place, at any radius. An arc form: the curved surface seen from close, spanning the frame bottom, with the phone point on its crest. A gravity well form: curved grid lines dipping under Earth, deep near the surface and shallowing with height, with a height marker that can slide up the well.

A GPS satellite, flat: a box body in surface with crescent shading, two solar panels in field2 with accent2 cell lines, an antenna dish facing Earth, and a small clock face slot on its body. States: idle (muted), named (body edge in accent while spoken), dim, broadcasting (rings pulse out from the antenna at a steady rate), on_rocket (seated on a small two-stage rocket for the launch, with a flame that can fire). Sizes from a 24 px point in the constellation to a 360 px close-up.

The constellation around the Earth disc: tilted elliptical orbit rings in line at low opacity, each split into a back half (behind Earth) and a front half, satellites placed on them by phase and travelling with time (one ring, then the six that fill the sky, about four satellites each, never a count label of its own). A trace state draws one ring bright in accent as a satellite runs it. A radius line from Earth's surface to one satellite with a tag anchor at its middle; a period arc along one ring with a tag anchor.

Signals: a travelling pulse (a short bright arc of wavefront in accent2 with a soft glow) that moves from a point to a point at a given progress, with up to two riding chips (a position pin chip, a time stamp chip with a tiny clock); concentric broadcast rings; a light beam streak (a long thin accent2 line with a bright head) for the speed of light; a bent path (refracts slightly crossing a band) and a bounce path (reflects off an anchor).

The ranging machinery of the cross-section: a range line from a satellite to a point (label anchor at its middle); a circle around a satellite through a point, drawn by the range line sweeping round, with a radius offset parameter so every circle can swell or shrink together by the same amount; the overlap ring of two circles drawn as a thin tilted ellipse through their two crossing points (a sphere-meets-sphere ring in the flat picture); candidate point markers (bright accent2 discs that can dim or glow); a blurred patch where swollen circles no longer meet (a soft neg tinted region); a snap to one point. Circles in line at mid opacity, the one named in accent.

A flat clock face (ink face ring, surface fill, crescent shading) whose hands are driven by time with a rate and an offset parameter: steady, off (an offset it cannot know), behind, ahead, in_step, and set_slow (a small knob on its rim turns back). A microsecond chip slot beside it. Small form (about 60 px) for tags and badges, large form (about 280 px) for the clocks station. Atomic and quartz differ by finish (atomic: a fine ring of tick marks; quartz: plain, a slight wobble), never by a logo.

kit.notes: No people, no hands, no faces anywhere (the brief: people only with a designed flat-cosmos character kit; none is declared). Flat-cosmos tokens only: field and field2 for the night, surface and surface2 for bodies, ink for type, muted and line for quiet parts, accent (orange) for the one element the narration names, accent2 (gold) for signals and light, accent4 (teal) only for the blue dot and the phone's point on Earth (its identity colour throughout), neg only for errors (the patch, the drift). Crescent shading, radius 26 on cards, stroke 4, offset shadow. Type: labels 24 to 30, body 30 to 36. Every on-screen word is the script's on_screen text, nothing else. Numbers only as the script states them.

scenes.world: the clocks station with a launch

design.treatment: The clocks station: Earth, the ground clock bottom-right, and the satellite now on a small rocket on Earth's surface with its clock beside it. The clock's knob turns back (set slow) with the tag set slow before launch; the rocket fires and rises along a dashed arc to the orbit; in orbit the clock's hand falls into step with the ground clock's. At centre a mini phone shows the drifted red dot sliding back home and turning teal.
design.why_motion: the fix happens before launch and pays off in orbit

scenes.subject: The chain in one breath

design.treatment: The cross-section returns and replays its own images fast, each on its words, with a tag landing on the thing it names: satellites pulse out (broadcast); a stamped pulse falls and the readout timer stops (travel time); three circles grow and meet (spheres meet); satellite D's circle arrives and all four snap to one point (fourth satellite).
design.why_motion: the recap is the lesson's own pictures, in order

scenes.subject: Real life adds noise: the dot is an estimate

design.treatment: The city skyline along the bottom, the air band above it, the phone at right with its map. A gold signal comes down from above and bends slightly as it crosses the air band; a second one bounces off the tall tower before reaching the phone. On the phone the teal dot grows a soft halo.
design.why_motion: the bend and the bounce are the noise, seen happening

beat_sheet.action: a signal bends crossing the air band

the halo grows round the dot

scenes.subject: Each time it appears, the phone has solved a timing problem
scenes.world: the phone, the city, the satellites above

design.treatment: The phone's dot pulses as in the opening; the halo tightens into it and the dot lands. A slow pull back: the city lights brighten and small satellites pass slowly above the skyline, each pulsing once. The final frame holds.
design.why_motion: the opening image returns, now understood
references: flat-cosmos pack: a lift at the close
